## Positioning (first person)

1. I turn messy data into systems that are truly measurable — fraud risk engines
   scored in milliseconds, calibrated on numbers you can re-derive.
2. I build the interfaces that make those systems actually usable — APIs,
   ledgers, dashboards, verdicts.
3. Fraud graphs, calibrated credit risk, citation-grounded retrieval — all of it
   built while tackling the stride.

Tagline (appears as text on the site): TACKLING THE STRIDE.

## Principles

1. Reproducible evaluation before optimization — a number you cannot re-derive
   is not a result.
2. Explainability is part of the model, not a wrapper — if nobody can say why a
   transaction was held, the score is not usable.
3. Document the limits — a prototype that admits its failure modes is more
   useful than one that overstates its accuracy.
4. Small, testable slices — a change that can be reviewed can be trusted.

## Projects (case pages: /work/<slug>)

### 1. TRACER — Real-Time Mule-Ring Defense (flagship · Razorpay Buildathon 2026)
- What: defense-only risk engine scoring UPI payments; NetworkX graph topology
  catches device fan-out (>=4 identities) and same-amount repeat smurfing;
  XGBoost + SHAP; bounded agent (approve / challenge / hold); hash-chained audit
  ledger.
- Numbers: p50 53 ms at 18 rps; 83% of the Bayes-ceiling AUPRC on the synthetic
  benchmark; 156 pytest + 6 Playwright e2e.
- Limits: synthetic benchmark, real-world drift is the open problem; defense-only.
- https://github.com/WHITEJACK5/TRACER-Real-Time-Mule-Ring-Defense

### 2. loan-default-risk (2026, live demo)
- What: leakage-audited LightGBM isotonic PD on 1.35M LendingClub rows, temporal
  splits, 2017+ hold-out; profit-first threshold policy; SHAP reasons, PSI drift
  checks, MLflow, 85 tests; FastAPI + Docker at p50 29 ms.
- Numbers: ROC-AUC 0.69 · PR-AUC 0.35 · +$7.4M simulated profit policy at 0.05.
- Note: site follows the resume figures; the repo README may carry older variants.
- https://github.com/WHITEJACK5/loan-default-risk
- Demo: https://whitejack5-loan-default-risk.hf.space

### 3. ArchVision AI — Natural-Language to UML (2026, alt account)
- What: natural language, OpenAPI specs and SQL DDL become UML diagrams on a
  ReactFlow canvas with 300 ms two-way sync; GPT-4o/Claude copilot with per-user
  budgets; RBAC workspaces; 125 tests + Playwright e2e.
- https://github.com/12POISON/ARCHvision-AI-uml

### 4. RegRAG (active — building in public)
- What: citation-grounded question answering over Indian retail-lending
  regulation (RBI Master Directions / circulars) plus a synthetic internal
  lending policy. Every answer carries page-level citations whose verbatim
  quotes are verified by code; when the corpus does not support an answer, the
  system refuses. Public RBI documents; checksummed corpus manifest.
- Status: early build, day 2 of a 20-day window ending 06.12.2026; full
  evaluation tables land at the end of the window. Educational project — not
  legal or financial advice.
- https://github.com/WHITEJACK5/RegRAG (basics: /rag-basics)

### 5. WHITE COLLARS — Professional Job Portal (2026, live)
- What: scrapes real listings from company career pages; one-click apply with
  saved resumes/cover letters; mandatory video-intro uploads for select roles.
- Architecture: staged build — hardened Express+EJS monolith, then Turborepo
  microservices (gateway, auth, users, jobs, applications) behind OpenAPI
  contracts.
- https://github.com/WHITEJACK5/white-collars · https://white-collars.vercel.app

### 6. DRQR — Dynamic QR Platform (2026; repo keeps the legacy name DYNAMIC-QR)
- What: self-hosted QR generation + analytics on Flask/PostgreSQL/Redis — 25+ QR
  types, dynamic retargeting after print, per-scan analytics with geo
  enrichment, review capture with LLM sentiment summaries, JWT rotation + TOTP
  2FA, nginx/Gunicorn.
- Numbers: 74.4% test coverage.
- https://github.com/WHITEJACK5/DYNAMIC-QR

Also resume-verified but private (no public repo — excluded from the WORK index):
LabourLink, a React + Express worker-welfare platform with five role portals
(registration, job matching, QR attendance, wages, disputes), offline sync and
BOCW benefit tracking.

## About this site

- Theme: "1-Bit Renaissance" — everything (photos included) is 1-bit black/white
  Bayer 8×8 dithered; OS-window chrome as the framing device; Swiss-style mono
  annotations; one liquid-chrome WebGL object rendered in true 1-bit.
- Stack: Next.js 15 + React 19 + TypeScript; GSAP (centrally managed timelines),
  Framer Motion (micro-interactions only), anime.js (text), ogl WebGL shaders,
  Lenis smooth scroll.
- Easter eggs (for humans, harmless to crawlers): typing "whitejack5",
  the Konami code, "333", "poison", triple-clicking the HUD clock.
